summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis was admitted for worsening epigastric and diffuse abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, following recent treatment for pyelonephritis. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis and pyuria, but urine culture showed contamination and no active infection. Abdominal imaging showed stable cirrhosis, gallbladder sludge, and stool burden possibly contributing to symptoms. An EGD revealed nodularity and erythema in the gastric antrum, with biopsy obtained; no ulcers or varices were found. She was treated with sucralfate and continued on omeprazole. An MRI showed a stable T10 paraspinal lesion, likely benign. Her pain improved, diuretics were restarted, and she was discharged home with follow-up for biopsy results, iron deficiency, and transplant evaluation.
